summary: Richard von Garbe was an Indology and philosophy scholar who studied under Rudolf von Roth and Bhagavata Acharya. He served as Lehrstuhlinhaber at the University of Tübingen from 1895 to 1927, succeeding von Roth.
Richard von Glahn is a sinologist and historian. He became a professor at the University of California, Los Angeles around 1987 and was a visiting fellow at the University of Tokyo from 1988 to 1989.

Riika J. Virtanen is a Tibetologist who completed doctoral studies at the University of Helsinki. Her supervisors included Asko Parpola, Klaus Karttunen, and Hannu Riikonen, and she also studied under Sangye Tandar Naga.

Rikizan Ishikawa was a Buddhist studies and Japanology scholar who studied at Komazawa University. He later taught there as a lecturer around 1978 and served as Professor of Buddhist Studies until 1997.
Ringu Tulku is a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies and under the traditional teacher Dilgo Khyentse Rinpoche.

Rinzin Thargyal was a scholar of Tibetology and history/archaeology. He completed his Magister degree at the University of Oslo by 1985, studying under supervisors Fredrik Barth and Arne Martin Klausen.

Rita Langer is an Indologist and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at SOAS, the Postgraduate Institute of Pali and Buddhist Studies, and the University of Hamburg (PhD 2004). She held a post at the University of Bristol (attested 2009).

Rita M. Gross was a religious studies and Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Chicago (~1965–1975). She served on the faculty at the University of Wisconsin-Eau Claire from circa 1979 to 2007.
Rizong Rinpoche was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies figure who studied under Tenzin Gyatso, the 14th Dalai Lama. He served as abbot of Gyume Tantric College (attested 1980).

Rob Linrothe is a historian, Tibetologist, and Buddhist studies scholar educated at the University of Minnesota and University of Chicago (PhD). He held posts at Skidmore College (1992–2009) and Northwestern University (2010–2022).

Rob Nairn is a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of London, King's College London, and the University of Zimbabwe. He later held posts at the University of Zimbabwe and the University of Cape Town.

Robert A. F. Thurman is a scholar of Tibetology, Buddhist studies, and religious studies who earned his PhD from Harvard University. He held professorships at Amherst College (1973, 1976) and became a director at Columbia University in 1988.

Robert Aitken was a Buddhist and religious studies scholar who studied at the University of Hawaii, UC Berkeley (~1947–1949), and Ryutaku-ji (~1950) under Daisetz Teitaro Suzuki. He held a post at the University of Hawaii.
Robert Alan Goodding is an Indology and religious studies scholar who earned his PhD from the University of Texas at Austin in 2002 under the supervision of Patrick Olivelle.

Robert B. Ekvall was a Tibetologist. He worked at the University of Chicago as a research associate in anthropology (~1951), at the University of Washington (1958), and at the Burke Museum of Natural History and Culture (attested 1983).
Robert Barnett is a Tibetologist who studied at the University of Cambridge. He served as a professor at Columbia University from circa 1998 to 2018.

Robert Caesar Childers was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics scholar who studied at Wadham College and under Yataramulle Dhammarama. He served as Professor of Pali and Buddhist Literature at University College London from circa 1872 to 1876.
Robert Chalmers was an Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics scholar who studied at Oriel College from 1877 to 1881. He later served as Master of Peterhouse, Cambridge from circa 1924 to 1931.

Robert Chambers was an Indologist who studied at Lincoln College (~1754–1758). He held posts at the University of Oxford (~1762–1773), as Chief Justice of the Supreme Court of Judicature at Fort William (~1791–1798), and president of the Asiatic Society (~1797–1799).

Robert Charles Zaehner was a scholar of religious studies, Iranian and Central Asian studies, and Indology who studied at Christ Church (~1933–1937). He served as Spalding Professor of Eastern Religions and Ethics at Oxford from circa 1952 to 1974.
